# A customer overpayment recorded as an ordinary transaction.
#
# Not through a `payment:` block, so nothing puts it in a lot: the credit on
# the receivable is simply a split someone wrote. The money itself went into
# the USD bank, and that is the split that carries the cost basis — one lump
# of currency, listed once, sellable from where it is held. The credit facing
# it records the obligation to give it back.
#
# What this fixture produces: `fx-balances` lists 100.00 USD at 1.4 CAD/USD on
# Assets:Bank:USD, and nothing on the receivable. The same answer the lotted
# prepayment in fx_refund_usd_prepayment.txt gets, which is the point:
# `lot_owner:` says which side of a receivable a split is, not how much
# currency the book holds.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Accounts Receivable USD
	type: Accounts Receivable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:USD
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"

2026-02-01 * "Customer overpaid, recorded by hand"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:USD 100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.40"
		value: "140.00"
	Assets:Accounts Receivable USD -100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.40"
		value: "-140.00"
